question.text: Yamuna Capital AIF values investee Bharat Metals on NAV basis. Equity share capital = INR 2 crore; General reserve = INR 10 crore; Revaluation reserve = INR 3 crore; Capital Redemption Reserve = INR 5 crore; P&L surplus = INR 4 crore. Number of shares = 20 lakh. What is the book NAV per share (cash net worth basis per PDF Illustration 11.4)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the PDF Illustration 11.4 footnote, cash net worth EXCLUDES revaluation reserve. Tangible NAV = Equity capital + General reserve + CRR + P&L surplus = 2 + 10 + 5 + 4 = INR 21 crore. NAV per share = 21,00,00,000 / 20,00,000 = INR 105 per share. The Trap: INR 120 includes revaluation reserve (adding INR 3 cr = INR 24 cr / 20 lakh = INR 120); INR 100 excludes both revaluation and CRR; INR 115 mis-treats CRR. Revaluation reserve is specifically excluded in cash net worth calculation. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical NAV math. XXI-B tests book value per share for listed PSU stocks. XV (Research Analyst) exam tests the full tangible-book vs reported-book distinction. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat II debt AIFs valuing collateralised distressed equity, NAV-based floor valuation (excluding goodwill and revaluation reserve) is the IPEV-recommended conservative anchor. Independent valuers will haircut your NAV further if intangibles look inflated.
